programme.title: Wild Sky
programme.desc: Scan the Australian skies, which regularly deliver some of the world's most volatile weather. Await cooling monsoon rains, watch lightning ignite vast wildfires, and marvel at the ingenious adaptations that help wildlife deal with these extremes.

programme.title: Wild Sky
programme.desc: Experience the powerful, colourful phenomena that swirl across the heavens in North America. Watch polar bears search for food under the aurora borealis, map the frigid path of a polar vortex, and elude violent tornadoes with a prairie dog family.

programme.title: Wild Sky
programme.desc: Observe the eternal search for water that defines the lives of Africa's wild animals. Witness the biggest marine feeding frenzy on Earth, see how cobras stock up on solar power, and join wildebeest herds and elephant clans on their epic migrations.

programme.title: Wild Side of the Moon
programme.desc: Explore how lunar phases set the rhythm for an endless contest between predator and prey. Soar by moonlight with colugos, gorge on a shellfish feast with macaques, and watch a prowling pride of lions try to turn a baby elephant into dinner.

programme.title: Alien Abyss
programme.desc: Get acquainted with an array of ocean oddballs and learn how billions of years' worth of changes, from ice ages to asteroid strikes, have shaped their looks and skills. Meet blind worms who fish, walking sharks, tree-climbing crabs, and much more.

programme.title: Alien Abyss
programme.desc: Feel the love in the strange-but-heartwarming partnerships between some of Earth's oddest creatures. Dive deep to see strange animals, from snapping shrimp to wolf eels, offer a hand to their fellow ocean-going weirdos to ensure mutual survival.

programme.title: Alien Abyss
programme.desc: Channel your inner sci-fi fan and explore the bizarre mating rituals of the ocean's most peculiar creatures. Learn how bloody battles for mates, gender bending and supersize litters of babies just might secure a next generation for these animals.

programme.title: Animal Senses
programme.desc: The sense of touch is useful to feel physical forces such as bites, changes in temperature and texture. Some animals have become extra sensitive to very faint vibrations, which gives them a lot of information about their environment.

programme.title: Africa's Hidden Kingdoms
programme.desc: This documentary looks at the wildlife of The Drakensberg Mountain range. We take a look at how creatures survive in the hostile landscape, from the highest peaks to the rolling grasslands below.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: The shadowy forests of Yala National Park are the perfect hideout for secretive leopards. It's time for one young female, Asha, to strike out alone. Join her as she fights for her own territory, finds a mate, and becomes a mother.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: Every year, the biggest elephant congregation in Asia occurs in Minneriya National Park. Here in this sacred place, baby Loka is born. Watch as he learns to suckle, swim and handle his trunk among the mêlée of giants that make up his family.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: Sri Lanka's lowlands are dotted with thousands of seemingly peaceful lakes, but don't be fooled, this is the realm of the mugger crocodile. Muggers are hunters from day one. Watch as these supreme predators compete with each other in the fierce heat.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: A manmade lake in Minneriya National Park supports the largest concentration of elephants in Asia. Follow a young male who has reached a turning point toward adulthood. In the rainforest, jungles teem with a variety of bizarre species of insects.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: Monsoon storms sweep over the tropical island of Sri Lanka, and water carried in with swirling mists hits the mountainous heartland, beginning a journey through the many changing faces of the island's forests.

programme.title: Island Of The Monsoon
programme.desc: Yala National Park is an avian Eden, home to 215 species of bird. This paradise offers many possibilities for parents who can weather the ever-changing climate. Every species must either raise their offspring here or find a new home before the dry season ends and the monsoon storms begin.

programme.title: Cub Camp
programme.desc: Spy on the summer cubs as they learn to climb trees and forage for food in preparation for their release into the wild. Get surprised by a set of new arrivals, observe the annual pre-hibernation eating binge, and enjoy a bear-friendly Thanksgiving.

programme.title: Cub Camp

programme.title: Supersenses
programme.desc: Vision - it's how ninety-five percent of animals interpret the world. Every species on Earth is a chapter in the fascinating story of sight. This episode follows that story from blurry beginnigs to mind-blowing hexnocular vision.

programme.title: Supersenses
programme.desc: See the animals that push the limits of physics, chemistry and engineering to pull off feats that humans can only dream of, and find out how evolution granted them with such amazing abilities. Sometimes it takes a super-power just to survive.

programme.title: Supersenses
programme.desc: Dive into a dazzling world beyond human perception, where animals use their super senses to detect light we can't see, sound we can't hear and even stranger forces we can't begin to detect.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: The Hudson Bay lowlands are part of North America's largest wetland. Over 300,000 square kilometers of muskeg, a vast bogland as far as the eye can see characterized by water soaked peat, mosses and stunted trees. Once thought of as barren wasteland, it is now understood that these bogs are crucially important to life on earth. Globally, there is as much carbon dioxide held in wetlands as there is in the atmosphere. The peatland ecosystem is the most efficient carbon sink on the planet.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: The Yukon is a true wilderness, one of the last on Earth. The vast land got its name from its longest river, which the Gwich'in, one of the indigenous people of the region, call "Yu-kun- ah", or, the "great river". The third longest waterway in North America, the Yukon River flows through wide open valleys and narrow channels over 3,000 km Northwest towards the storm tossed Bering Sea.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: It's November at Cape Tatnam. Winter is coming to the lower Western shore of Hudson Bay. But the ice - which should be forming on Hudson Bay by now - is nowhere to be seen. 2016 has been the warmest year on record. In late November, the temperature is 10 degrees warmer than its average. Climate change is wreaking havoc across the North. At just below zero degrees Celsius, the sea cannot freeze.

programme.title: The Agenda
programme.desc: A weekly talk-show looking beyond the headlines and “accepted wisdom” to find the real story. Hosted by award-winning journalist and presenter Stephen Cole, The Agenda quite simply sets The Agenda . You won't find the same-old talking heads recycling platitudes; instead thought-provoking guests to debate and explore key issues of today's world. Using virtual reality graphics to bring subjects to life, Stephen will navigate through subjects ranging from “Prove That Climate Change Exists” to “Who Will Win the Race to Space”. Opposing views will be given opportunity to flourish and develop into a meaningful conversation. The Agenda: No nonsense talk; Challenging perceptions.

programme.desc: Middleweights man the marquee as UFC returns to the Meta APEX in Las Vegas on Sunday, October 11 as Brendan “All-In” Allen squares off with “CLD” Christian Leroy Duncan. A rankings staple for the last several years, Allen has forced his way into the Top 5 on the strength of a three-fight winning streak over Marvin Vettori, Reinier de Ridder, and Edmen Shahbazyan. Gloucester, England's Duncan has claimed five straight victories heading into his first UFC main event assignment, most recently out-hustling former title challenger Jared Cannonier in July.

programme.title: (L) UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott - Main
programme.desc: Returning to Edmonton for the fourth time, UFC brings an action-packed fight card to Rogers Place on Sunday, October 18 headlined by a compelling welterweight main event between Joaquin “New Mansa” Buckley and “Proper” Mike Malott. Buckley makes his first trip north of the border seeking to maintain his place in the welterweight Top 10 and showcase the explosive skills that previously produced wins over former title challengers Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington. The Ontario native Malott makes his seventh consecutive start in Canada and second main event appearance of 2026, looking to add to his four-fight winning streak and build on his third-round stoppage win over Gilbert Burns in Winnipeg back in April.

programme.title: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott - Main
programme.desc: Returning to Edmonton for the fourth time, UFC brings an action-packed fight card to Rogers Place on Sunday, October 18 headlined by a compelling welterweight main event between Joaquin “New Mansa” Buckley and “Proper” Mike Malott. Buckley makes his first trip north of the border seeking to maintain his place in the welterweight Top 10 and showcase the explosive skills that previously produced wins over former title challengers Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington. programme.title: (L) UFC 333: Volkanovski vs. Evloev - Main
programme.desc: UFC's annual October showcase in Abu Dhabi has historically been packed with action, and this year is no different as a pair of highly anticipated championship fights close out UFC 333 at Etihad Arena. In the main event, two-time featherweight champion Alexander “The Great” Volkanovski defends his title for the second time this year, taking on the challenge of undefeated Russian contender Movsar Evloev. And in the co-main event, bantamweight rivals battle for a third time as two-time titleholder Petr “No Mercy” Yan squares off with former champion Merab “The Machine” Dvalishvili to determine which of them will lord over the 135-pound weight class heading into next year.
